questions.html:
Which of the following statements about datagrams sent by a node in a network using $\textsf{IPv4}$ protocol is (are) true?

  1. Datagrams at the source must be the size of the smallest maximum transmission unit (MTU) of all the links on a path to the destination.
  2. Datagrams may be fragmented during routing.
  3. Datagrams are reassembled only at the destination.
questions.solution:
Answer: D

Official discussion page

questions.html:
The figure below shows a network with a NAT router.  

  • In step $1,$ host $10.0.0.1$ sends a datagram from its port $3345$ to host $128.119.40.186$’s port $80.$ The router will use the NAT translation table to determine the source and destination IP addresses and port numbers of the datagram it will forward.
  • In step $2,$ the destination IP address and port number of the outgoing datagram are provided for you.

Determine the source IP address and port number of this datagram.
questions.solution:

questions.html: Consider a packet with a total length of $250$ bytes (including $\textsf{IPv} 4$ header, with no options) and an id field equal to $17,$ sent from a host $\text{A}$ to a host $\text{B}$, passing through routers $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$. Assume that the subnet where host $\text{A}$ is connected has an MTU of $500$ bytes, the subnet where host $\text{B}$ is connected has an MTU of $80$ bytes and the subnet between $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ has an MTU of $120$ bytes. Assuming that the $\text{“don't fragment"}$ flag is not set, how many fragments does router $\text{X}$ divide the packet into?

A network of $4$ routers $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ is arranged as shown below. The routers use the distance vector routing, using the number of hops as the metric. The value  $\text{“8”}$  is used by all routers to indicate "infinity" (to conclude that a router is unreachable).

In each round, all nodes exchange their distance vectors with their respective neighbours. Then all nodes update their distance vectors. In between two rounds, any change in cost of a link will cause the two incident nodes to change only that entry in their distance vectors.

The link $\text{C-D}$ goes down. How many exchanges would it require for each of them to conclude that $\text{D}$ is unreachable?
questions.solution:
Answer: C

questions.solution:

questions.html:
Suppose that host $\mathrm{A}$ is connected to a router $\mathrm{R} 1, \mathrm{R} 1$ is connected to another router, $\mathrm{R} 2$, and $\mathrm{R} 2$ is connected to host $\mathrm{B}$.
Suppose that a TCP message that contains $900$ bytes of data and $20$ bytes of TCP header is passed to the IP code at host $\text{A}$ for delivery to $\text{B}.$
Assume that:

  • link $\text{A-R1}$ can support a maximum frame size of $1024$ bytes including a $14$-byte frame header,
  • link $\text{R1-R2}$ can support a maximum frame size of $512$ bytes, including an $8$-byte frame header
  • link $\text{R2-B}$ can support a maximum frame size of $512$ bytes including a $12$-byte frame header.

Let IP header size be $20$ bytes.
The length of the last fragment at each of the three links respectively are:
questions.solution:
Answer: D
